0.reason: the regression this case guards is caught by the age assertion on the next line, which the reviewer measured failing with the fix reverted (assert 0.0 >= 7140); the ordering assertion is a description of the expected output rather than the guard, so no further repair round is spent on it

findings.text: assert [row['node'] for row in rows] == ['own-old', 'own-recent'] does not redden on the regression the case is written to catch, so the ordering clause its docstring claims ('lead by that age', :382) is carried only by the age assertion below it. I measured this rather than inferred it: with the fix reverted the added case alone fails at :410 (assert 0.0 >= (7200 - 60)), not at :409, because when both rows fall back to a zero age the sort key at reckon/crew/needs_you.py:193 ties and the node-name tiebreak ('own-old' < 'own-recent') reproduces the expected order anyway. The regression is still caught by :410 and by the own-old 2h00m token at :414, so this is not blocking; the assertion should compare the order only after asserting a non-zero age gap, or the docstring should claim only the age. The landing fragment's claim that the case asserts the elder 'leads the row order' (fragments/the-monitor-shows-the-work-it-watches/the-follower-lists-your-runs-that-need-you.html:4) inherits the same overstatement.
